The operator said "Reject anything else"; the agent's rule added "with 4xx"; the "obey verbatim" header made that paraphrase law, so S9 returned 400 and failed A6. Keeping the operator's words beside the rule, and flagging what the rule adds in every digest, puts the source in front of each later session at zero extra calls. payload.chose: 1.2 CONTRACT (rule fidelity). (a) decision_logged gains `quote?`: the operator's own words the rule came from, copied exactly, non-empty, at most 300 chars, valid only alongside `rule` (the guard pattern). (b) A pure core/rule-fidelity.ts lists a rule's SPECIFICS: HTTP status codes and classes (400, 4xx), paths (a token with `/` between word characters, or a file name with an extension), and values (backticked spans, double-quoted spans, tokens carrying a digit). It then reports the specifics the quote lacks, by case-insensitive whitespace-collapsed substring. (c) Standing constraints renders each quoted rule as `- [D<n>] <rule> — operator: "<quote>"`, plus ` (not in the operator's words: <specifics>)` when any are missing. The header becomes `Standing constraints — obey verbatim; where a rule quotes the operator, the quote decides (<N>):` ONLY when an in-force rule carries a quote, so quote-less records render byte-identically. decisions.md and the review packet render the quote too. (d) sofar_log_decision returns `warnings[]`, and `sofar event append --type decision_logged` prints them, naming the unquoted specifics; never a refusal. (e) The `rule` and `quote` descriptions and the CLI dialect's fields teach: word the rule as the operator did, and pass their words as quote. Guard notices in hooks are unchanged in 1.2.
payload.over: Refusing a rule that adds specifics (a paraphrase that rightly names a file would cost a retry, and the plan says warn); recording prompts so the quote can be verified mechanically (user content in the record); rendering the quote instead of the rule (the operator's sentence often lacks the context the rule supplies); clipping long quotes at render (a clipped quote can drop the clause that matters, so the cap sits at validation)

A read is the first moment the path is known, and it comes before the edit. Measured on this repo (all initiatives): file tokens in chose, over and rule name 74 real files from 92 in-force decisions (30 ruled), median 1 decision per file, 8 files above 3. Directory tokens alone spread over 375 files, and adding `because` adds evidence mentions, not subjects. So the surface is precise and small, and told-once keeps a session's cost to a few hundred chars, which is where the tokens +<1% prediction comes from. The wording follows Claude Code's hook docs: text framed as out-of-band system commands can trigger prompt-injection defenses, so write factual statements. Today's guard notice is imperative.

2.1 CONTRACT (read-time surfacing, B1).
(a) WHEN. PostToolUse also tests every path a call READS: Claude Code Read (tool_input.file_path) and Grep (tool_input.path when it names a file, plus tool_response.filenames when present, first 5); Cursor Read (file_path, else path; the live payload is checked before 2.1 is marked done); and on every host's shell call (Claude and Codex Bash, Cursor Shell) the operands that name an existing regular file inside the repo root, resolved against the hook's cwd, first 5, flags skipped. Edits keep their paths. Paths under .sofar/ or outside the root are never tested. Matchers: Claude PostToolUse becomes Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash|Read|Grep; Cursor postToolUse becomes Shell|Write|Read; Codex is unchanged. A read appends NOTHING to the record.
(b) WHAT. In-force decisions from EVERY initiative that either GUARD the path (a path: guard matches, as in record-index 3.2) or NAME it (a file token in chose, over or rule, using rule-fidelity's path class, that equals the path's tail at a / boundary). Directory tokens and `because` are not scope. In force mirrors the fold: a superseded decision is out (a ruled target falls only to a ruled superseder), and so is any until-scoped decision, since task resolution is not indexed. Edit-time guard notices stop asserting superseded rules too.
(c) ORDER AND CAP. Guards first (other initiatives before this one, as today), then ruled mentions, then unruled mentions. Within a tier, the longer matched tail wins, then the newest. Stored relevance (typed-judge D10) only reranks within a tier and adds; its reader lands with typed-judge 5.1. At most 3 decisions per call, then `…and N more decisions name <path> — sofar find <path>`. Rules render verbatim with the operator's quote (drift-hardening D2, memory-lead D2). chose and over render as heads cut at the first clause boundary, as the digest does (memory-lead D4).
(d) TOLD ONCE per (session, decision, path). The set lives in the derived index at .sofar/.index/told/<session>.json and is disposable: a lost file re-tells, never silences. Read and edit notices share it. SessionStart with source compact or clear empties it. The edit notice keeps its lastTouch suppression.
(e) WORDED AS FACTS. Guard: `sofar: <path> is governed by [<handle>], a standing rule: "<rule>" (guard: <guard>). Work against it needs a decision that supersedes <handle>.` Ruled mention: `sofar: [<handle>] names <path>. Its standing rule: "<rule>".` Unruled mention: `sofar: [<handle>] <date> names <path>: chose <head> over <head>.` record-index D2 holds: only a guard says "governed by". The edit notice takes the guard wording and drops "obey it verbatim".
(f) INDEX. guards.json becomes the decision-scope tier: per initiative, each decision with a guard or a file mention, carrying ordinal, ts, rule, quote, guard, heads, mention tokens and a superseded flag. INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bumps. Still one refresh per hook call.
